# A staged vessel placeholder is unstamped, so its pane is re-created

## Context

A behaviour regression introduced by `#18667`, found while the swarm traced an operator report of duplicated "Moving pane to another window…" load masks. Reproduced and A/B-controlled in the unit tier before this ticket was filed.

**Corrected 2026-09-13, and the correction matters more than the original framing.** This ticket first said the operator's masks were caused by `#18667`, and I told @neo-opus-grace to stand her `#18664` suspect down on that basis. @neo-gpt-emmy then matched the operator's screenshot host to a temporary export of @neo-gpt's `#18674` header work built on `7bd4db9f74` — **before** `#18667`, carrying the old unguarded pairing — so that frame cannot be evidence about this change. Her two real-pointer controls pass identically before and after the repair, and @neo-opus-grace's headed titlebar arm passes at both heads with zero stand-ins.

**So the scope of this ticket is the measured behaviour change, not the operator's symptom.** Nobody has reproduced the operator's masks. The unit A/B below is the only positive control. Whatever produces the reported frame is a separate open question and is not closed by this ticket.

`#18621` is closed and does not get reopened; this is its follow-up.

## The Problem

`VesselEmbodiment.stage()` swaps the departing pane for a stand-in at the same index of the pane's own parent, which for a docked pane is the tab's card container:

```
sourceParent.removeAt(sourceIndex, false, true);
sourceParent.insert(sourceIndex, placeholder, true);
```

That stand-in is created as `Neo.create(VesselPlaceholder)` with **no config**, and `dockItemId` appears nowhere in `VesselPlaceholder`. So an unstamped component legitimately occupies `body.items[index]` — the exact array `Reconciler#reconcileTabChrome` zips against the tab bar's `dockItemIds` to decide which live component is which item.

`#18667` made that zip conditional. An unstamped component now pairs by position **only while the two arrays agree in length**. When they diverge, the stand-in is no longer recognized, the host is asked for the item, the host makes a new component, and the original stand-in stays parented where it was.

**A/B, same probe and fixture, only `Reconciler.mjs` swapped:**

| Reconciler | lengths agree | lengths diverge |
|---|---|---|
| pre-`#18667` `3044d7f86b` | pairs the stand-in, body 2 | **pairs the stand-in, body 2** |
| merged `4add999757` | pairs the stand-in, body 2 | **asks the host, second component created, body 3, stand-in left behind** |

Two masks and an embodiment that never settles is the *shape* of the reported symptom, which is why the swarm followed it here. The resemblance is not evidence: the reported frame predates this regression, so this A/B stands on its own as a measured behaviour change and not as an explanation of that report.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselEmbodiment.mjs:54` — `const placeholder = Neo.create(VesselPlaceholder);`. `itemId` is already in scope: `stage()` is declared `({itemId, windowId} = {})`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselPlaceholder.mjs` — declares `ntype`, `baseCls`, `isLoading` and `role`. Zero occurrences of `dockItemId`.
- `src/dashboard/dock/projection/Reconciler.mjs#reconcileTabChrome` — builds its live-item map from `bar.sortZoneConfig.dockItemIds` × `body.items[index]`, and that map outranks the caller's `resolveItem`.
- **One site only.** The proxy embodiment in the same file creates a drag proxy from a caller-supplied config and uses it as the projection *target*, never as a body stand-in. This is not a two-path fix.
- **Nothing committed could have caught it.** Three e2e specs touch the mask — `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL:732`, `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL:560`, `WorkstationTearOutSourceContinuityNL:495` — and each asserts presence or styling of a single match. No arm anywhere counts stand-ins or asserts exactly one. The twenty `DockVesselEmbodiment` unit arms are all green at the merged head.

## The Fix

**Stamp the stand-in with the item it stands in for**, at the creation site, so it pairs by identity rather than by a count. `itemId` is already in scope one line above.

Stated as a hypothesis rather than a conclusion: it is one line, it leaves the predicate alone, and it should satisfy both of the conflicting requirements below — but it is unrun at filing time and the implementer owes the measurement, not the reasoning.

**Why the predicate cannot be fixed instead, and this is the load-bearing constraint.** Two requirements meet at identical predicate inputs with opposite required outcomes:

| Requirement | unstamped + lengths diverge |
|---|---|
| `#18621`'s shipped arm — a drifted bar must not hand one item another item's pane | must **not** pair |
| This regression — a stand-in genuinely belongs to the slot it occupies | must **pair** |

No widening or narrowing of the length guard satisfies both. The discriminator has to be identity, which puts the fix at the creator. An implementer who reaches for the predicate will red one arm to green the other.

## Contract Ledger

Added at @neo-gpt-emmy's review reading: the repair changes what a documented, agent-and-consumer-facing lookup returns, so it owes a ledger rather than only a diff.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.dashboard.dock.Workspace#resolveLivePane` | `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs`, the method's own docblock, which states that stand-in exclusion is by CATEGORY and never one instance at a time | The cross-window stand-in class joins the three classes already excluded: buttons, rail tabs and projection placeholders. A stamped stand-in is never returned as the live pane for the item it stands in for | None. A pure predicate over an existing match set; when no live pane exists the method already returns `null` | The clause carries its reason inline, in the same voice as the three siblings | Measured before the clause existed: the lookup returned the load mask itself as the live pane. Arm "a stand-in never answers for the live pane it replaced" holds it, including the case where a real pane sits beside the stand-in |
| A `VesselPlaceholder` instance created by `VesselEmbodiment.stage()` | `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselEmbodiment.mjs`, the creation site, where `itemId` is already in scope | Carries the departing item's `dockItemId`, so a projection can recognize it in the slot it occupies rather than inferring from position | None. Previously it carried no identity at all, which is the defect | The creation site states why identity is required and that live-pane readers exclude the class | Arms "the staged stand-in names the item it stands in for" and "a stand-in staged into a tab body keeps its slot when the bar ids and the body have diverged", both red first |

Retirement: both rows retire together if stand-in identity ever becomes a declared config on the placeholder class rather than a creation-site argument.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — restores intended behaviour; no public contract is added or removed. The ledger above records a behavioural narrowing of an existing protected method, not a new surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: a staged stand-in is recognized by the projection when the bar's id list and the body have diverged in length — the host is not asked for that item and no second component is created.
- [ ] AC-2: red-first — an arm places an unstamped-today stand-in in a tab body with a length divergence and reds on `4add999757`, then greens on the fix. Presence assertions do not satisfy this; the arm counts.
- [ ] AC-3: `#18621`'s arm stays green — a drifted bar with ordinary unstamped panes still refuses to pair, and `#18667`'s same-length conflicting-stamp arm stays green too. Both conflicting requirements hold in one run.
- [ ] AC-4: the twenty `DockVesselEmbodiment` arms and the workstation unit folder stay green.
- [ ] AC-5: the mechanism is named in the PR body with its measurement. A fix whose mechanism is unnamed does not close this.
- [ ] AC-6: no stand-in is left behind in any window after a completed cross-window transfer, measured headed on a real two-window arrangement. Reachable on the branch rather than deferred past merge. **This does not claim to resolve the operator's reported masks.** That symptom's provenance is a temporary export built before the regression existed, nobody has reproduced it, and this ticket closes without it. If the headed witness later reproduces it, that is a new finding and gets its own ticket rather than being folded back in here.

## Out of Scope

- Reverting `#18667`. The pairing repair it delivered is the fix for a silent mis-binding and is not traded away for this; if @tobiu wants `dev` clean before a repair lands, that is a separate operator call.
- `#18674`'s stack-handle work in the same function, which @neo-gpt owns and is editing today.
- The proxy embodiment path, which mints no stand-in.
- Styling of the placeholder, settled by the closed `#18414`.

## Avoided Traps

| Rejected explanation | What falsified it |
|---|---|
| The close routine's settle step (`#18664`). | The A/B above: identical fixture, only `Reconciler.mjs` swapped, and the duplication follows the file. |
| Widen or relax the length guard. | `#18621`'s arm requires the opposite outcome at identical inputs. One predicate cannot serve both. |
| It is a two-path fix covering the proxy embodiment too. | The proxy is built from a caller-supplied config and used as the target, never inserted into a body as a stand-in. |
| The existing coverage would have caught a real regression here. | Twenty embodiment arms green at the merged head, three e2e mask arms assert only presence or styling of a single match, and nothing counts stand-ins. |
